newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says Jan-May car sales up 9.2 percent. [CORRECTED 11:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: VW says Jan-May car sales up 9.2 percent. [CORRECTED 11:05 GMT]

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Wednesday its group vehicle sales for the the first five months of 1997 rose 9.2 percent to 1.8 million units.

VW, the largest carmaker in Europe, also said group car deliveries rose 6.8 percent to 1.1 million units in the period from January to May. VW sells vehicles under the VW, SEAT, Skoda and Audi brand names.
VW management board chairman Ferdinand Piech said in the text of a speech at an employee meeting that about 1.1 million VW brand vehicles were delivered during the period, a gain of 6.8 percent.

But Piech said sales in Germany, VW's top European market, slumped 10.8 percent to about 238,000 vehicles. Sales were also lower in western Europe, falling 4.4 percent (Corrects from 0.5 percent) to 595,000 units.
Piech said in the speech that VW would be successful in the long-term only if the group kept up measures to improve productivity.
